subject: math
title: Differential Equations
syllabus: Ordinary differential equations, their order and degree, the solution of differential equation by the method of separation of variables, solution of a homogeneous and linear differential equation of the type dy/dx + p(x)y = q(x).

body: An equation linking x, y and derivatives of y. A solution is a function that makes it true; a condition like y(0) = 1 picks one curve from the family.
Order = highest derivative present. Degree = power of that derivative once the equation is a polynomial in the derivatives.
Forming the equation of a family with n constants: differentiate n times and eliminate the constants.
If \f{dy}{dx} = f(x)g(y): \f{dy}{g(y)} = f(x)dx, integrate both sides, then use the condition for C.
Exact forms: x dy + y dx = d(xy), \f{x dy − y dx}{x^{2}} = d(\f{y}{x}), \f{x dy − y dx}{x^{2} + y^{2}} = d(tan^{−1}\f{y}{x}).
Homogeneous (every term the same degree): put y = vx, then separate v and x.
\f{dy}{dx} + P(x)y = Q(x). Multiply by the integrating factor μ = e^{∫P dx}:
If the equation is linear in x instead, swap roles: \f{dx}{dy} + P(y)x = Q(y).
Bernoulli \f{dy}{dx} + Py = Qy^{n}: put u = y^{1−n} to make it linear.
Many JEE questions only need μ(x)y at two points: compute μy at the start, add ∫μQ between them.
Look for a derivative hiding in the equation: (1 + x^{2})y' + 2xy = ((1 + x^{2})y)'.
Substitutions like t = tan x or u = x + y + 2 turn awkward equations into standard ones.

traps: Do not forget the constant C — the condition fixes it.
Integrating factor uses P with the + sign form y' + Py = Q.
Degree is undefined if a derivative sits inside sin, log, e^{…}.
After y = vx, dy/dx = v + x dv/dx, not just v.
Check which variable the equation is linear in.
A solution can blow up before the asked point — watch tan and 1/(…).

pyq.q: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation \f{dy}{dx} + 2y sec^{2}x = 2 sec^{2}x + 3 tan x · sec^{2}x such that y(0) = \f{5}{4}. Then 12(y(\f{π}{4}) − e^{−2}) is equal to ____.
sol: Put t = tan x: \f{dy}{dt} + 2y = 2 + 3t; integrating factor e^{2t}.

pyq.q: Let g be a differentiable function such that ∫_{0}^{x}g(t)dt = x − ∫_{0}^{x}tg(t)dt, x ≥ 0 and let y = y(x) satisfy the differential equation \f{dy}{dx} − y tan x = 2(x + 1) sec x g(x), x ∈ [0, \f{π}{2}). If y(0) = 0, then y(\f{π}{3}) is equal to
sol: Differentiate: g(x) = 1 − xg(x) → g(x) = \f{1}{1 + x}. The equation becomes y' − y tan x = 2 sec x.

pyq.q: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation \f{dy}{dx} + 3(tan^{2}x)y + 3y = sec^{2}x, y(0) = \f{1}{3} + e^{3}. Then y(\f{π}{4}) is equal to
sol: 3 tan^{2}x + 3 = 3 sec^{2}x: y' + 3y sec^{2}x = sec^{2}x. In t = tan x: \f{dy}{dt} + 3y = 1.

pyq.q: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation (x^{2} + 4)^{2}dy + (2x^{3}y + 8xy − 2)dx = 0. If y(0) = 0, then y(2) is equal to
Let the solution y = y(x) of the differential equation \f{dy}{dx} − y = 1 + 4 sin x satisfy y(π) = 1. Then y(\f{π}{2}) + 10 is equal to ____.
sol: Integrating factor e^{−x}: y = −1 − 2(sin x + cos x) + Ce^{x}.

pyq.q: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation \f{dy}{dx} + \f{2x}{(1 + x^{2})^{2}}y = xe^{\f{1}{1 + x^{2}}}; y(0) = 0. Then the area enclosed by the curve f(x) = y(x)e^{−\f{1}{1 + x^{2}}} and the line y − x = 4 is ____.
If y = y(x) is the solution of the differential equation \f{dy}{dx} + 2y = sin(2x), y(0) = \f{3}{4}, then y(\f{π}{8}) is equal to :
Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation (1 + x^{2})\f{dy}{dx} + y = e^{tan^{−1}x}, y(1) = 0. Then y(0) is
sol: Integrating factor e^{tan^{−1}x}: (ye^{tan^{−1}x})' = \f{e^{2tan^{−1}x}}{1 + x^{2}} → ye^{t} = \f{e^{2t}}{2} + C (t = tan^{−1}x).

pyq.q: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation (2x log_{e}x)\f{dy}{dx} + 2y = \f{3}{x}log_{e}x, x > 0 and y(e^{−1}) = 0. Then, y(e) is equal to ____.
sol: Divide by 2x log x: y' + \f{y}{x log x} = \f{3}{2x^{2}}; integrating factor log x.
(y log x)' = \f{3 log x}{2x^{2}} → y log x = −\f{3}{2}·\f{log x + 1}{x} (the constant is 0 from y(e^{−1}) = 0) → y(e) = −\f{3}{e}.

pyq.q: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation (x^{2} + 1)y' − 2xy = (x^{4} + 2x^{2} + 1)cos x, y(0) = 1. Then ∫_{−3}^{3}y(x)dx is :
Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation x\f{dy}{dx} − y = x^{2} cot x, x ∈ (0, π). If y(\f{π}{2}) = \f{π}{2}, then 6y(\f{π}{6}) − 8y(\f{π}{4}) is equal to :
sol: (\f{y}{x})' = cot x → \f{y}{x} = log sin x + C; y(\f{π}{2}) = \f{π}{2} gives C = 1.

pyq.q: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation sec x \f{dy}{dx} − 2y = 2 + 3 sin x, x ∈ (−\f{π}{2}, \f{π}{2}), y(0) = −\f{7}{4}. Then y(\f{π}{6}) is equal to:
Let x = x(y) be the solution of the differential equation y^{2}dx + (x − \f{1}{y})dy = 0. If x(1) = 1, then x(\f{1}{2}) is :
sol: Linear in x: \f{dx}{dy} + \f{x}{y^{2}} = \f{1}{y^{3}}; integrating factor e^{−1/y}.

pyq.q: If x = f(y) is the solution of the differential equation (1 + y^{2}) + (x − 2e^{tan^{−1}y})\f{dy}{dx} = 0, y ∈ (−\f{π}{2}, \f{π}{2}) with f(0) = 1, then f(\f{1}{√{3}}) is equal to :

Let y = f(x) be the solution of the differential equation \f{dy}{dx} + \f{xy}{x^{2} − 1} = \f{x^{6} + 4x}{√{1 − x^{2}}}, −1 < x < 1 such that f(0) = 0. If 6∫_{−1/2}^{1/2}f(x)dx = 2π − α then α^{2} is equal to ____.
Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation (xy − 5x^{2}√{1 + x^{2}})dx + (1 + x^{2})dy = 0, y(0) = 0. Then y(√{3}) is equal to
Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation 2 cos x\f{dy}{dx} = sin 2x − 4y sin x, x ∈ (0, \f{π}{2}). If y(\f{π}{3}) = 0, then y'(\f{π}{4}) + y(\f{π}{4}) is equal to ____.
sol: y' + 2y tan x = sin x; integrating factor sec^{2}x: (y sec^{2}x)' = sin x sec^{2}x → y sec^{2}x = sec x + C.

pyq.q: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation cos x(log_{e}(cos x))^{2}dy + (sin x − 3y sin x log_{e}(cos x))dx = 0, x ∈ (0, \f{π}{2}). If y(\f{π}{4}) = \f{−1}{log_{e}2}, then y(\f{π}{6}) is equal to:
sol: Put u = log cos x (du = −tan x dx): u^{2}\f{dy}{du} = 1 − 3yu, i.e. \f{dy}{du} + \f{3y}{u} = \f{1}{u^{2}} → yu^{3} = \f{u^{2}}{2} + C.

pyq.q: If for the solution curve y = f(x) of the differential equation \f{dy}{dx} + (tan x)y = \f{2 + sec x}{(1 + 2 sec x)^{2}}, x ∈ (−\f{π}{2}, \f{π}{2}), f(\f{π}{3}) = \f{√{3}}{10}, then f(\f{π}{4}) is equal to :
sol: Integrating factor sec x: (y sec x)' = \f{sec x(2 + sec x)}{(1 + 2 sec x)^{2}} = \f{1 + 2 cos x}{(cos x + 2)^{2}} → y sec x = \f{sin x}{cos x + 2} + C.

pyq.q: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation: \f{dy}{dx} + (\f{6x^{2} + (3x^{2} + 2x^{3} + 4)e^{−2x}}{(x^{3} + 2)(2 + e^{−2x})})y = 2 + e^{−2x}, x ∈ (−1, 2), satisfying y(0) = \f{3}{2}. If y(1) = α(2 + e^{−2}), then α is equal to:
sol: The coefficient is \f{d}{dx}log\f{x^{3} + 2}{2 + e^{−2x}}, so the integrating factor is \f{x^{3} + 2}{2 + e^{−2x}} and (IF · y)' = x^{3} + 2.

pyq.q: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation x^{4}dy + (4x^{3}y + 2 sin x)dx = 0, x > 0, y(\f{π}{2}) = 0. Then π^{4}y(\f{π}{3}) is equal to :
If the solution curve y = f(x) of the differential equation (x^{2} − 4)y' − 2xy + 2x(4 − x^{2})^{2} = 0, x > 2, passes through the point (3, 15), then the local maximum value of f is ____.
sol: With u = x^{2}: (u − 4)(12 − u) is largest at u = 8 → 4 × 4 = 16.

pyq.q: If a curve y = y(x) passes through the point (1, \f{π}{2}) and satisfies the differential equation (7x^{4} cot y − e^{x} cosec y)\f{dx}{dy} = x^{5}, x ≥ 1, then at x = 2, the value of cos y is :
sol: Multiply by sin y: with u = cos y, \f{du}{dx} = −sin y\f{dy}{dx} gives \f{du}{dx} + \f{7u}{x} = \f{e^{x}}{x^{5}} — linear.

pyq.q: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation (x + y + 2)^{2}dx = dy, y(0) = −2. Let the maximum and minimum values of the function y = y(x) in [0, \f{π}{3}] be α and β, respectively. If (3α + π)^{2} + β^{2} = γ + δ√{3}, γ, δ ∈ Z, then γ + δ equals ____.
sol: u = x + y + 2: u' = 1 + u^{2}, u(0) = 0 → u = tan x → y = tan x − x − 2 (increasing).

pyq.q: If the solution y = y(x) of the differential equation (x^{4} + 2x^{3} + 3x^{2} + 2x + 2)dy − (2x^{2} + 2x + 3)dx = 0 satisfies y(−1) = −\f{π}{4}, then y(0) is equal to :
If the solution y(x) of the given differential equation (e^{y} + 1)cos x dx + e^{y} sin x dy = 0 passes through the point (\f{π}{2}, 0), then the value of e^{y(π/6)} is equal to ____.
sol: The left side is d[(e^{y} + 1) sin x] = 0 → (e^{y} + 1) sin x = 2.

pyq.q: Let y = y(x) be the solution curve of the differential equation sec y\f{dy}{dx} + 2x sin y = x^{3} cos y, y(1) = 0. Then y(√{3}) is equal to :
sol: Divide by cos y: sec^{2}y y' + 2x tan y = x^{3}; with t = tan y this is linear: t' + 2xt = x^{3}.

pyq.q: Let α|x| = |y|e^{xy − β}, α, β ∈ N be the solution of the differential equation xdy − ydx + xy(xdy + ydx) = 0, y(1) = 2. Then α + β is equal to
sol: Divide by xy: d(log\f{y}{x}) + d(xy) = 0 → log|\f{y}{x}| + xy = log 2 + 2.

pyq.q: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation (1 + y^{2})e^{tan x}dx + cos^{2}x(1 + e^{2 tan x})dy = 0, y(0) = 1. Then y(\f{π}{4}) is equal to :
sol: Separate: \f{dy}{1 + y^{2}} = −\f{e^{tan x}sec^{2}x}{1 + e^{2 tan x}}dx → tan^{−1}y = −tan^{−1}e^{tan x} + C, C = \f{π}{2}.

pyq.q: The solution curve, of the differential equation 2y\f{dy}{dx} + 3 = 5\f{dy}{dx}, passing through the point (0, 1) is a conic, whose vertex lies on the line :
The solution of the differential equation (x^{2} + y^{2})dx − 5xydy = 0, y(1) = 0, is :
sol: Homogeneous: y = vx gives x\f{dv}{dx} = \f{1 − 4v^{2}}{5v} → −\f{5}{8}log|1 − 4v^{2}| = log x (C = 0 from y(1) = 0).

pyq.q: If the curve y = f(x) passes through the point (1, e) and satisfies the differential equation dy = y(2 + log_{e}x)dx, x > 0, then f(e) is equal to:
sol: log y = ∫(2 + log x)dx = x + x log x + C; at (1, e): C = 0.
At e: log y = 2e → y = e^{2e}.

pyq.q: Let y = y(x) be the solution curve of the differential equation (1 + sin x)\f{dy}{dx} + (y + 1)cos x = 0, y(0) = 0. If the curve y = y(x) passes through the point (α, −\f{1}{2}), then a value of α is :
sol: The equation is d[(1 + sin x)(y + 1)] = 0 → (1 + sin x)(y + 1) = 1.

pyq.q: Let x = x(y) be the solution of the differential equation 2y^{2}\f{dx}{dy} − 2xy + x^{2} = 0, y > 1, x(e) = e. Then x(e^{2}) is equal to :
sol: Bernoulli in x: put u = \f{1}{x}: \f{du}{dy} + \f{u}{y} = \f{1}{2y^{2}} → uy = \f{1}{2}log y + C.

pyq.q: Let a curve y = f(x) pass through the points (0, 5) and (log_{e}2, k). If the curve satisfies the differential equation 2(3 + y)e^{2x}dx − (7 + e^{2x})dy = 0, then k is equal to
Let x = x(y) be the solution of the differential equation y = (x − y\f{dx}{dy})sin(\f{x}{y}), y > 0 and x(1) = \f{π}{2}. Then cos(x(2)) is equal to :
sol: Homogeneous: x = vy gives −y\f{dv}{dy} sin v = 1 → cos v = log y + C, C = 0 (v = \f{π}{2} at y = 1).
At y = 2: cos\f{x}{2} = log 2 → cos x = 2(log 2)^{2} − 1.

pyq.q: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation \f{dy}{dx} = (1 + x + x^{2})(1 − y + y^{2}), y(0) = \f{1}{2}. Then (2y(1) − 1) is equal to
sol: At x = 1 the right side is \f{11}{6} → 2y − 1 = √{3} tan\f{11√{3}}{12}.

pyq.q: Let the solution curve of the differential equation xdy − ydx = √{x^{2} + y^{2}}dx, x > 0, y(1) = 0, be y = y(x). Then y(3) is equal to
sol: Homogeneous: y = vx gives \f{dv}{√{1 + v^{2}}} = \f{dx}{x} → v + √{1 + v^{2}} = x.

pyq.q: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation x\f{dy}{dx} − sin 2y = x^{3}(2 − x^{3})cos^{2}y, x ≠ 0. If y(2) = 0, then tan(y(1)) is equal to
sol: Divide by cos^{2}y; with t = tan y: xt' − 2t = x^{3}(2 − x^{3}) → (\f{t}{x^{2}})' = 2 − x^{3}.

pyq.q: The differential equation of the family of circles passing the origin and having center at the line y = x is :
sol: Circles x^{2} + y^{2} − 2ax − 2ay = 0. Differentiate: a = \f{x + yy'}{1 + y'}.

pyq.q: Suppose the solution of the differential equation \f{dy}{dx} = \f{(2 + α)x − βy + 2}{βx − 2αy − (βy − 4α)} represents a circle passing through origin. Then the radius of this circle is :
sol: A circle's slope is −\f{x − h}{y − k}: no y on top means β = 0; then \f{(2 + α)x + 2}{−2α(y − 2)} needs \f{2 + α}{2α} = 1 → α = 2.

pyq.q: Let f(x) be a positive function such that the area bounded by y = f(x), y = 0 from x = 0 to x = a > 0 is e^{−a} + 4a^{2} + a − 1. Then the differential equation, whose general solution is y = c_{1}f(x) + c_{2}, where c_{1} and c_{2} are arbitrary constants, is :
